violated_contract: A rollout of a workload that holds scarce, autoscaled capacity (GPU nodes that a stockout can make unobtainable) must never leave that capacity unclaimed while replacements do not yet exist. Each node may be released only to its own replacement. A strategy that stops every old pod and creates replacements only after the slowest one exits (Kubernetes Recreate) leaves idle nodes for as long as one hung drain lasts; the cluster autoscaler returns them after its unneeded-node timer, and in a stockout they cannot be bought back. A pod-count floor does not protect them, because the rollout itself removed the pods it counts.
canonical_prevention: The batch-pipeline-worker chart renders every worker Deployment with RollingUpdate, maxSurge 0 (no surge GPU) and a bounded percentage maxUnavailable, so each replacement is created as soon as its predecessor is told to stop and takes the freed node seconds after that pod exits. The preserve-live image-only helper admits only Recreate or RollingUpdate with an explicit zero maxSurge. The batch-pipeline-pool node minimum equals the HPA floor (operator-managed, in the capacity runbook).
